activeTailKernel.classification: all-order induced-l1 bound: fixed charge columns are uniform in every admissible degree and the final sector contains all s>=S

largeChargeSector.proof: write x=s/j in [0,2]; for q>=0 use abs(s-q)/(s+q)<=1 and abs(i*x-q)<=max(q,abs(2*i-q)); for q=-1 use (s+1)/(s-1)<=(S+1)/(S-1)

allOrderTheorem.coverage: every bivariate input monomial has j>=1 and s/j in [-1,2]; the two endpoints are the actual degree-one monomials Z and W
allOrderTheorem.degreeReduction: at either endpoint every factor (i+j)/(i+j-1) decreases with j, so the maximum over every input degree is attained at j=1
allOrderTheorem.slopeReduction: for fixed j the complete absolute column sum is convex in x=s/j on [-1,2], so its maximum is attained at x=-1 or x=2
allOrderTheorem.strictTailProof: for i>N and -1<=q<=2i, divide each endpoint factor by the B_r input weight i; the maxima occur at q=2i for x=-1 and q=-1 for x=2, then both expressions decrease with i

candidateComparison.meaning: the finite candidate remains outside the proved disk and is not certified as a singularity

negativeControl.classification: failure of the present sufficient active-tail inequality only; the exact polynomial transport endpoint bound still passes, and this is not evidence of nonanalyticity or a singularity

restartCertificate.statement: there is a unique degree-greater-than-80 active correction; triangular formal uniqueness identifies it with the canonical active series, and the exact two-endpoint transport Neumann bound constructs canonical U and V at the same radius

scope.classification: all-order Banach-space theorem, exact rational degree-80 restart certificate, and finite exact implementation regressions
limitations: the active correction theorem remains restricted to q>=-1
the transport endpoint theorem uses the isotropic weighted Wiener norm
the nearby negative control fails only the present active-tail bound
the result concerns the reduced edge generating equation rather than the full PDE
the R0.32 finite Pade candidate remains outside the certified fixed-charge disk
no Navier-Stokes regularity or blow-up conclusion is claimed
scope.result: an exact all-order two-endpoint theorem for normalized transport and a larger common analytic radius for the reduced fields

transportKernel.classification: all-order two-endpoint bound for the polynomial center plus the unknown strict-tail correction
